gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the current Alpine iLX-W770-M sells for $499.95 at World Wide Stereo on 2026-11-08, only $48.05 under the $548.00 Sony XAV-AX6000 at the same store. ChatGPT's 'best compact upgrade' card showed $399.99, and CarAudioNow names the iLX-W770-M with no price.
standout_why: I compared against CarAudioNow's 'Best Car Stereos & Head Units (Tested)' (cited, updated August 2026) and World Wide Stereo's 'Best Car Stereos of 2026' (top result, 2026-08-28). CarAudioNow already prices the AX6000 ($548 Amazon, $598 Crutchfield), the DMH-WT6000NEX ($899.99), the XAV-9000ES ($998), the DMX958XR ($1,099 Crutchfield), the JVC KW-M795BW ($499) and the KMM-X705 ($219). It names the Alpine iLX-W770-M but gives no price, and it does not cover the Sony XAV-AX3200/AX3700/AX8100 or the Kenwood DMX4710S/DMX5710S ladder at all. I couldn't check the two cited Crutchfield pages: crutchfield.com and crutchfield.ca both returned HTTP 403 to my fetch. So this score assumes they don't price the W770-M either.
decides: This confirms the Sony XAV-AX6000 as the pick. At today's dealer prices the Alpine iLX-W770-M is not a cheaper 'compact' option: it costs $48.05 less than the AX6000. Sony's own range has cheaper steps down: the XAV-AX4000 at $448 (CarAudioNow: 2 V preamp and resistive screen, against the AX6000's 5 V), the XAV-AX3700 at $348 and the XAV-AX3200 at $298, which World Wide Stereo calls 'Best Value'. For a 10.1-inch screen, the Pioneer DMH-WT6000NEX costs $899.99 and its preamp is weaker (4 V and 14 W RMS ×4 against 5 V and 20 W RMS ×4, per CarAudioNow).
